subject: Computer Networking
title: Network Energy Consumption
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Network Energy Consumption.

hook.text: The internet uses about 10% of global electricity. As data grows, so does the energy bill.

buildup.text: Data centers and network gear consume massive power. Cooling alone is 40% of a center's energy.

discovery.text: Energy per bit drops with newer chips. But total traffic grows faster than efficiency improves.

twist.text: AI training is power-hungry. One model run can use as much energy as 100 homes in a year.

climax.text: Renewable data centers, liquid cooling, and smarter hardware aim to bend the energy curve.

punchline.text: The internet's carbon footprint grows. Efficiency alone won't fix it.

quiz.question: Why doesn't improving energy efficiency per bit solve the internet's energy problem?
options: Total traffic is growing faster than efficiency improves
Energy efficiency has reached its physical limit
New protocols use more energy than older ones

details.summary: The global networking infrastructure consumes approximately two to three percent of world electricity, growing with traffic. Energy-efficient hardware, intelligent sleep modes, renewable energy sourcing, and optimized routing algorithms are critical for sustainable growth of digital infrastructure.
details.whyItMatters: Exponential traffic growth makes network energy consumption an environmental and economic challenge. Efficiency improvements directly reduce the carbon footprint of the digital economy.
takeaways: Networking consumes 2 to 3 percent of global electricity
Traffic growth threatens to outpace efficiency improvements
Sleep modes and adaptive speeds reduce idle power consumption

faq.question: What consumes the most energy in networks?
faq.answer: Data centers and access networks each account for roughly a third of network energy use. Mobile base stations are major consumers due to radio transmission power. Core network equipment is more efficient per bit but handles enormous traffic volumes.

faq.question: How can network energy consumption be reduced?
faq.answer: Equipment sleep modes power down unused ports and line cards. Adaptive link speeds match capacity to actual traffic. More efficient hardware generations improve performance per watt. Traffic optimization reduces unnecessary data movement.
